chunks: As for whatever is in it from Wuhayb ibn Hafs, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh—may Allah be pleased with him—from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamdani, from Wuhayb ibn Hafs al-Kufi, known as al-Mantuf.

key_terms.الْكُوفِيِّ: the Kufan; indicating affiliation with Kufah
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفِ بِالْمَنْتُوفِ: known as al-Mantuf; a distinguishing epithet for the narrator
key_terms.عَنْ وُهَيْبِ بْنِ حَفْصٍ: from Wuhayb ibn Hafs; the narrator whose transmission path is being clarified
key_terms.فَقَدْ رَوَيْتُهُ: I have narrated it; the compiler’s declaration of transmission

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Wuhayb ibn Hafs in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits narrations from Wuhayb ibn Hafs. It serves as a chain-authentication notice in the book, identifying the intermediaries linking the compiler to this Kufan narrator.
